scope: scripts/qualify_composite_capture.py on a frozen Debug build of 99a3709 (D:\wp\sr04), 57/57 steps, in one owned scratch CPU 1511-1 PN V4.1 with a second CPU on one subnet, an S7 connection, PID_Compact 3.0 and a virtual TO_PositioningAxis 10.0 (each added with checkpoint, compile and save). A project review saved with project_snapshot_capture is captured into one composite phase: AutomationML (cax_export, retained and reopened through automationml_inspect/automationml_reopen), connections (one connection review whose observation rows equal connection_inspect), drives (drive_observe returns no drives: native, no records) and technology (one technology-profile record per saved technology object whose relationship rows equal technology_read's exposed slots), all native, composable, untruncated and changing nothing in the project. A malformed reviewId refuses as InvalidRequest and an unknown one as ArtifactUnavailable. A fresh owned Portal reopen captures the same content; after the S7 connection is deleted and its checkpoint restored, the recovered copy at another path refuses the original review as ProjectMismatch and captures the same content from its own new review.
limitations: No drives (drive capture is drive_observe's empty result; Startdrive cannot read a new drive's drive objects), no TO hardware-module or channel connection and fewer than 32 records, so truncation is not reached.
The capture is not an atomic project revision; freshness and source authenticity stay unverified, as the result states.

composite_engineering_rebind_plan is not qualified by this run: over the fixture and recovered phases it reports no broken connection, because no verified flow creates a declared TO hardware relationship to break.
